test_focus: per-prompt CONTENT routing. Phase 17 found per-prompt WRAPPER routing didn't help. Phase 20 confirmed EC > CH on decision-shaped scenarios. Phase 21 tests the smaller intervention: keep the neutral wrapper, but swap the seed CATEGORY per call based on the prompt's classified domain.
tester: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context), live as the developer

module_changes: bog_agents_cli/dreamscape/imagination.py — _route_content_category_for_request() + per-call category filter in _maybe_inject, with fallback to unfiltered when no match
Dreams generated from Phase 21+ carry a `category:` field in their frontmatter
tests_cover: Empty result when filter matches nothing
Pre-Phase-21 dreams (no category field) excluded when filter is on
Middleware filters end-to-end on decision-shaped prompts
Middleware falls back to unfiltered archive when no match

arms: Static — sample from any dream (no filter). Phase 16 shipped engineering default behavior.
Per-prompt routed — classify the prompt, sample from EC dreams when prompt is engineering, myth dreams when prompt is creative/decision-shaped.
experiment_design.archives: Both arms get the SAME mixed archive: 3 engineering-craft dreams + 3 myth dreams per agent.
experiment_design.judge_design: Sonnet 4.6 head-to-head, response order randomized per trial.
experiment_design.wrapper: Both arms use neutral wrapper. Only the seed CATEGORY differs.

aggregate.interpretation: Statistically indistinguishable from static. 95% CI [38.3%, 57.1%] straddles 50%. Point estimate slightly favors static (50.5%) but well within noise.

implications: **Per-prompt CONTENT routing does NOT improve outcomes at this N.** Aggregate routed win rate 47.6% with 95% CI [38.3%, 57.1%] — straddles 50%. The mechanism works correctly but doesn't pay off in measurable judge preference.

**The pattern is similar to Phase 17's wrapper-routing result.** Both per-prompt routing variants (wrapper and content) ship as mechanisms but don't auto-engage. The agent-level routing from Phase 11/12 is the load-bearing decision.

**Debugging-shaped routed wins (53%, slow-prod-query 67%) hint there's signal, but it's within noise at this N.** The single big winner (slow-prod-query at 67%) is suspicious — could be the prompt's 'designing' surface keyword tripping the classifier into creative routing, and the routed myth seeds happened to land for that prompt.

**Decision and creative routed-arm performance is essentially tied with static.** Myth seeds on decision-shaped technical prompts don't recreate the Phase 11 creative-prompt magic — likely because the agent voice is still engineering, not creative (the wrapper is also neutral).

**Release-note-voice at 33% is the biggest static win.** Routed used myth seeds; static sampled the mixed archive (some EC, some myth). For voice/copy questions, mixed sampling outperforms exclusive myth.

**Shipping decision: ship the mechanism, keep `use_content_routing=False` default.** Like Phase 17's per-prompt wrapper routing, content routing is preserved as a knob for future research and power-users who can A/B test on their workloads.

feature_verdicts.category_filter_mechanism: sings — 6 unit tests pass, end-to-end live verification works
feature_verdicts.per_prompt_content_routing_effectiveness: ambiguous-to-slightly-negative — routed 47.6% with CI [38%, 57%]. Mechanism works; outcomes don't measurably improve.
feature_verdicts.shipping_decision: ship the knob, default OFF. Like Phase 17, the per-call routing surface is preserved for future research.

known_limitations: N=15 per scenario means CI widths are 15-25pp. A larger trial (N=30+) could distinguish marginal effects.
The mixed archive (3 EC + 3 myth) is artificially balanced; real archives accumulate from real dreams over time and skew per the agent's domain preferences.
Decision-pattern detection over-triggers on surface keywords ('designing' → creative). An LLM-based prompt classifier (analog to Phase 19) could improve precision.
verdict: MIXED — mechanism solid, default keeps it off. The agent-level routing from Phase 11/12 (which Phase 14 + Phase 20 confirmed at N=140 and N=60 respectively) is the load-bearing decision. Per-prompt content routing is preserved as a knob.
next_steps: Phase 26 (suggested): N=30+ confirmation of the per-prompt content-routing finding. Phase 21's CI [38%, 57%] is wide; a tighter measurement would resolve whether the slight negative lean is real.
Phase 27 (suggested): use Phase 19's LLM classifier to drive per-prompt routing. The keyword classifier's surface-keyword false positives might be hurting routed-arm performance.
